vibe.rationale: Vibe 3. Down from 4 (May 27 evening). The Israel-Lebanon escalation on Day 12 of the 45-day ceasefire extension is the primary driver of this morning's vibe reduction. Waves of Israeli strikes across the Lebanese south — Tyre, Sidon (5 killed), Adloun (family fleeing, 6 killed), Tyre motorcycle (2 killed), Beirut southern suburb (Dahiyeh) — represent the most significant Israel-Lebanon deterioration since the extension was announced May 16. The Iran deal picture adds three compound negatives: (1) Trump 'will not be rushed' — explicitly extends deal latency horizon; (2) Oman threat ('blow them up') introduces a Gulf partner fracture signal; (3) Shamkhani Day 2 nuclear 'fantasy' challenge unresolved. PCE 3.3% core in-line is the most constructive element of the morning and prevents a drop to 2: the catastrophic >4.0% scenario that would have materially altered June FOMC calculus did not materialize. The case against 2: PCE in-line, deal alive (Khamenei endorsement stands, no counter-signal), overnight CENTCOM strikes within established self-defense pattern, no Brent spike above $107. The case against 4: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire breakdown is a genuine new negative reopening a second front, WPA T-1 creates irreversibility at midnight tomorrow, Trump 'won't rush' extends deal uncertainty, Shamkhani challenge unresolved, global PMI stalled. Vibe 3. Return to 4 requires: Israeli-Lebanese ceasefire holding signal plus Iranian FM formal nuclear text. Drop to 2 requires: Israeli strikes confirm ceasefire formal collapse with Hezbollah retaliation; Iranian counter-signal on nuclear framework; CENTCOM repositioning indicating May 29 offensive preparation.

items.headline: Iran Deal + WPA T-1: Trump 'Won't Be Rushed,' Threatens Oman; Overnight CENTCOM Strikes; Shamkhani Day 2 Unresolved; Hormuz Day 90 = WPA 90-Day Calendar Milestone
items.summary: The Iran deal and WPA picture entering May 28 morning carries four significant developments from Wednesday and overnight. First: Trump explicitly told reporters he 'will not be rushed' into a deal with Iran, adding that Iran's efforts to outlast him would fail because he doesn't 'care about the midterms.' This statement materially extends the deal uncertainty horizon and negates the 2-3 day countdown urgency from last week. Second: Trump issued a threat against Oman — 'Oman will behave just like everybody else or we'll have to blow them up' — following reports of a proposed arrangement in which Oman and Iran would jointly charge a toll for ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz. The toll proposal represents a novel deal architecture that departs from the Witkoff/Rubio framework; the Oman threat introduces a Gulf partner fracture signal. Third: overnight CENTCOM self-defense strikes on Iranian military targets and drones are confirmed — within the established operational pattern but notable given the deal-negotiation backdrop. Fourth: Shamkhani's May 27 evening declaration that US nuclear control is a 'fantasy' enters Day 2 unresolved — no Iranian moderating counter-statement has been issued. Araghchi: 'unsure if imminent.' Cumulative signal: the deal is alive (Khamenei endorsement stands; no counter-signal) but Trump's public posture has shifted from optimistic urgency to strategic patience. WPA hard deadline is 24 hours away. Today is the 90th day of the Hormuz conflict — the same number as the WPA hard ceiling — a symbolic convergence point. No emergency session. No pre-deadline House floor vote. Senate: 9 resolutions rejected; no 10th filed. Bipartisan House majority (Golden bloc) unactivated. Administration legal posture: 'hostilities terminated' — does not survive May 29 plain-text; naval blockade, CENTCOM strikes, and Hormuz closure remain operational. Deal not signed. Rubio meeting Pakistani FM on Friday May 29.

items.headline: CRITICAL: Israel-Lebanon Ceasefire Day 12 Fraying — Waves of Strikes Hit Tyre, Sidon (5 Killed), Adloun (6 Killed), Beirut Suburb; Second-Front Risk Returns to Active Matrix
items.summary: The most significant geopolitical development entering May 28 morning is the sharp Israeli escalation in Lebanon on Day 12 of the 45-day ceasefire extension. Israel launched waves of strikes across southern Lebanon and Beirut. Confirmed incidents: (1) Tyre — displacement order issued for eight buildings in the coastal city and surrounding neighborhoods; strikes followed. (2) Sidon — Israeli drone struck an apartment building housing displaced families; 5 killed, 21 wounded. (3) Adloun — Israeli drone struck a car carrying a fleeing family; 6 killed. (4) Near Tyre — drone strike on a motorcycle without warning; 2 killed. (5) Beirut southern suburb (Dahiyeh) — Israeli air strike; white smoke from residential area. Lebanon's health ministry aggregate: at least 11 killed including two children, 21 wounded (partial; incident-level exceeds this). Both sides accuse the other of ceasefire violations. The 2026 Israel-Lebanon ceasefire 'was supposed to have taken effect on 17 April but has never been fully observed' (Wikipedia). The 45-day extension (agreed May 16) was characterized at the time as 'second-front risk off' — that assessment is now compromised. This morning's Israeli strike wave is the most operationally significant since the extension was agreed. Analytical implications: (1) The second-front risk has returned to the active threat matrix — direct input to the Vibe 3 morning assessment. (2) The strike pattern — targeting Tyre, Sidon, displacement corridors, and Dahiyeh — is consistent with prior suppression-of-rocket-capacity operations, but at this intensity also consistent with preparatory suppression if an Iran nuclear site strike is in preparation (prior US official reporting on Israeli intentions carries forward). This is a HIGH UNCERTAINTY interpretation but within the established operational logic. (3) Hezbollah formal retaliation response is a key watch — any rocket barrage into northern Israel = ceasefire formally dead = second front open. CISA: clean streak Day 25 holds overnight.

items.headline: PCE Core 3.3% In-Line; Headline at 3-Year High; Q1 GDP Second Estimate Today; Warsh Day 14 First Major Inflation Test — No Statement Issued
items.summary: April Personal Consumption Expenditures released this morning at 8:30 AM ET — the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge and Warsh Day 14's first major data release as Chair. Core PCE (excluding food and energy) rose 3.3% YoY in April, in line with economists' forecasts. Headline PCE is at its highest in nearly three years, driven by Hormuz-derived energy cost embedding across gasoline, fuel oil, and transportation categories — the 90-day blockade's supply-chain impact is now fully embedded in the April baseline. CBS News headline: 'The first inflation report under new Fed chief Kevin Warsh shows prices at highest in nearly 3 years.' Analytical assessment: the core 3.3% in-line result avoids the catastrophic >4.0% scenario that would have materially altered June FOMC calculus. This is the most constructive economic data point of the morning and prevents a further vibe deterioration on the economic channel alone. However, headline-at-3-year-high reinforces the consumer affordability crisis — CNN Business reporting consumer sentiment at all-time low, worse than Great Recession or pandemic; bankruptcy filings rising three consecutive years; personal savings at three-year low. Warsh has issued no public statement on this PCE report or on his policy framework. June FOMC is 19 days away; the communication vacuum after two consecutive weeks of hot inflation data is itself a market signal. Q1 GDP second estimate releases today alongside PCE: the advance was +2.0% annualized (rebound from Q4 2025's +0.5%). Second estimate incorporates more complete trade flow, services consumption, and corporate inventory data. Key watch: PCE deflator revision direction — downward real growth with upward deflator confirms stagflation. Cleveland Fed Nowcast carried from May 28 evening prior filing: 4.18%. Fed funds: 3.50-3.75%; hold expected through June by consensus.

items.headline: NextEra/Dominion $67B AI Power Deal; Snowflake +37.5% AWS $6B; S&P Global PMI Stalls; Markets Enter Session Mixed
items.summary: Secondary economic developments. First: NextEra Energy is acquiring Dominion Energy in an all-stock deal valued at approximately $67 billion (announced May 18, 2026). The combined entity becomes the world's largest regulated utility and third-largest US energy infrastructure company. Strategic thesis is explicitly AI-oriented: meet surging data center electricity demand; use AI to drive construction and operations efficiencies. Bloomberg: NextEra is betting the Dominion deal can 'speed US infrastructure for AI.' This is the largest single bet on AI power infrastructure to date. Regulatory approval required from FERC, state public utility commissions, and shareholders. Completion timeline: 2027 at earliest. Second: Snowflake surged 37.5% in after-hours following better-than-expected Q1 earnings and a $6 billion, 5-year AWS spending commitment — continuing the AI infrastructure investment acceleration narrative into the morning. Third: S&P Global flash PMI surveys (May) show business growth stalled as the Middle East war exerts a growing economic toll. Europe hardest hit — UK and eurozone both in decline. US and Japanese economies have decelerated. First PMI reading to fully capture the 3-month war's supply chain and demand impact. Fourth: market context entering Thursday. US500 fell to 7,503 (-0.23% from prior session); Dow +220 at records (divergence reflecting rotation dynamics). Futures little changed entering Thursday open. Oregon gas: $5.35/gallon (2026 record, 4th highest nationally). National: $4.564.
